memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"That same night they are to eat the meat roasted over the fire, along with
bitter herbs, and bread made without yeast. Do not eat the meat raw or boiled in
water, but roast it over a fire-with the head, legs and internal organs. Do not
leave any of it till morning; if some is left till morning, you must burn it."
- Ex 12:8-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The meal itself was a sermon. Every element carried meaning.

Bitter herbs recalled the bitterness of slavery. God did not want them to forget
where they had come from. Freedom is sweeter when you remember the taste of
bondage. Bread without yeast was practical, because there was no time to wait
for dough to rise, but it also became a lasting symbol of separation from
corruption.

The lamb was roasted whole, not cut apart and boiled. It stayed one. And nothing
was to be left till morning. This was a meal for that night, eaten completely, a
once-for-all provision for a once-for-all deliverance.

John notices something at the cross. When the soldiers came to break the legs of
the crucified men, they found Jesus already dead and did not break His. John
writes that this happened so that Scripture would be fulfilled: "Not one of his
bones will be broken" (John 19:36), quoting the Passover regulation.

The whole Lamb. Nothing broken. Nothing left over. It is finished.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you remember what God saved you from, or have you grown comfortable?
2. Is there any "leftover" of the old life you are keeping just in case?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, help me never to forget the bitterness You rescued me from, and never to
hold back part of my life from You. Amen.
